articleTitle: Synchronous Generator Loss of Excitation Detection Technique Based on Waveforms Envelopes Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The synchronous generator is a machine widely used in electrical power system (EPS), which operates with constant frequency. Its fuctioning mainly depends on the continuous use of excitation systems that are susceptible to problems such as short-circuits, which can cause partial or total inactivity, causing the incorrectly operation of the machine. This state can cause irreversible damage to its structure and also to the electrical system to which it is connected. Several techniques have been proposed to detect the loss of excitation, among which the Mason and Berdy methods stand out, being widely used. Although these techniques present selectivity problems in some situations, leading to new techniques which are proposed to improve their performance in these situations. This work proposes a new methodology for detecting the loss of excitation (LOE) in synchronous generators, wich is based on the analysis of the envelopes of voltage and current signals waveforms. The proposed method has been tested for different operational conditions of the network, which were simulated in the ATPDraw software.

articleTitle: A Voltage Support Strategy Based on a Per-Phase Controlled Inverter in Faulty Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The independence of reactive current injection from the active power produced by distributed generators makes the inverters a key element in improving grid stability, particularly during grid faults. This paper proposes a new per-phase control strategy for three-phase inverters during asymmetrical and symmetrical grid fault conditions. The control strategy guarantees the safe operation of the inverter during voltage sags. As a result, the grid is better supported since the voltage at the point of common coupling is improved in each phase independently. In particular, this paper introduces a new control strategy to raise the Point of Common Coupling voltage based on the voltage reduction in each phase and to avoid undervoltage during grid fault conditions. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The simulations are carried through Matlab environment.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Analysis of the Loadability of a Transmission System with High Participation of Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Network congestion (loadability) depends on the maximum amount of electric power that can be sent through a transmission system while maintaining its normal operating conditions. This indicator can vary to the point of being critical. A case of this are the scenarios with the presence of wind non-conventional renewable energy sources (RESs) included within the transmission system networks. By presenting fluctuations that come from the nature of the wind speed, threats and technical repercussions are generated within the stability of the network, creating uncertainty about tension control, and affecting loadability. This paper proposes a probabilistic analysis of the loadability of a transmission system with high participation of RESs using the point estimate method (PEM) which allows to implement a complete and agile evaluation in computational terms of the different scenarios with different proportions of RES in the transmission network. In the development of the study of the affectation of the loadability in a power system due to the uncertainty generated by the inclusion of RES, the IEEE system 24 buses is taken as a case of study, where two-buses of thermal generators were exchanged for wind RES to analyze indicators such as the total load margin and the minimum voltage load margin for different power injection scenarios.

articleTitle: Stochastic Analysis (MCS) for Mitigation of Reliability Indicators of the Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The study aims to indicate the methodology of an algorithm to mitigate the supply reliability indicators through small-scale simulations with the IEEE 34 model through deterministic analysis of the Monte Carlo Method through Matlab, to calculate the SAIDI and SAIFI indicators independent of the problem caused in the distribution. The algorithm consists of analyzing the data and selecting the recloser and/or DG to serve the most consumers. The results show that the best results are with the activation of the DG at bar 890 of the model, where the SAIDI obtained a reduction of 57.88<sup>%</sup> and the SAIFI a reduction of 57.63%. Thus, the implementation of smart grid and DG systems by distribution system operators will improve the reliability of the power system. Thus, with the methodology applied on a large scale, to exemplify, in the reliability indicators of some South American countries, there are reductions, SAIFI from 17.6 to 7 events/year and SAIDI from 21.6 to 9.18 hours/year.

articleTitle: Voltage Variations Originated by the DG Anti-islanding Protection: Evaluation and Mitigation for Maintaining the Power Quality Indices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Anti-islanding protection (AIP) is an important part of the distribution system with distributed generation (DG). Therefore, this protection is required for security purposes. The voltage variations originated by the synchronous DG Antiislanding protection is a recent problem investigated which can violate the power quality (PQ) indices in a distribution system. Moreover, violation of power limits increases with the insertion of more distributed generators in the distribution network. This paper explores the voltage variations while DG anti-islanding protection is activated. Then, we perform a practical solution such as load shedding for maintaining the power quality within its limits, although this is a radical method for distribution companies. Finally, we discuss the results obtained.

articleTitle: A Proposal for Detection and Correction of Current Transformer Distorted Secondary Currents Due to Saturation Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: In some conditions, the increase of the magnetic flux in the current transformer (CT) core can lead to its saturation, which can generate many problems in the protection of Electric Power Systems (EPS). Due to this phenomenon, this work presents the development of an algorithm for the correction of the distorted waveform coming from the secondary of a saturated CT, which uses Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The analyzed signals were obtained via simulations from a test system in the ATPDraw software, where different saturation conditions were generated. The project was divided into two stages: detection and correction of saturation. In the detection step, a method based on the third difference function was developed. The methods were implemented in MATLAB software, in which the preliminary results point to a robust algorithm capable of reconstructing the distorted signal even in cases of severe saturation.

articleTitle: Electromechanical Wave Propagation Analysis in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Power system disturbances induce ElectroMechanical Waves (EMWs) that propagate through the transmission network with a velocity much smaller than the speed of the light, causing system instability that may lead to cascading failures and blackouts. Previous studies model nonlinear EMW propagation via partial differential equations while considering a uniform and nonuniform distribution of the moments of inertia of the synchronous generators and ignoring the parameters of lines. This paper considers a more realistic power system model by accounting for the line admittances when distributing the generator inertias, which is a key step of the EMW continuum modeling. Simulations carried out on the New England 39-bus 10-machine system revealed that the calculation of EMW velocity and also arrival time of disturbance are significantly improved using the new generator inertia distribution. The inertia distribution pattern also changed the EMW propagation path, providing a more accurate information for designing control signals to damp system oscillations due to disturbances.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Detect High Impedance Faults Using Time and Frequency Domains Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The detection of the high impedance fault (HIF) is a challenging task for power system engineers and, although there is an extensive number of publications on this topic, the HIF still has various characteristics to be exploited and means to make its distinction over the other system's occurrences. This paper presents a novel method for detecting HIF using characteristics in the time and frequency domains. The proposed method searches the buildup and shoulder stages using the positive peaks of the current signal to then analyze the third harmonic to detect the HIF. The test system used represents a radial power distribution feeder which was simulated in ATPDraw and the implementation of the method was made in Matlab®. The results shown that the proposed technique has great robustness detecting all HIF cases without operational errors for another transient events.

articleTitle: Reactive Consumption and Distributed Generation - Adequate Reactive Compensation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Distributed generation (DG) is an interesting alternative in the search for reduction of supply costs, but in addition to the classic care related to interconnection, equipment and the approval of the distributor's own access project, electric power quality should be highlighted, the power factor, harmonics, and harmonic resonance. The analyze study shows the consequences of PF with the insertion of DG-PV, from simulations in DIgSilent in three possible scenarios: Grid and DG, Grid and DG with capacitors, Grid and DG with antiresonance filter, as expected the THDv has an increase considered in scenario 2 compared to scenario 1, proving the need for the antiresonance filter, with the implementation of the filter the system will operate with THDv of 4.3%.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis in a Colombian Non-Interconnected Zone with BESS and PV Systems in Different Locations of a Recloser as Main Protection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Various areas of Colombia meet their energy needs from the generation of electricity with Diesel generators since they are not connected to the National Interconnected System (SIN for its acronym in Spanish). In some of these areas, generation systems have been installed from unconventional sources, whose characteristics make them ideal power systems to propose and evaluate different protection strategies and schemes. Due to the importance of maintaining the electrical service in these populations, in this work the installation of a recloser in different parts of the system is proposed to increase the reliability of the network in the event of failures in different parts of the distribution system and its stability is evaluated in the same way with the operation of these devices through RMS simulations.

articleTitle: Influence of the Frequency Estimator Response on Synchronous Generator Overexcitation Protection Performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Problems arising from the different operating conditions of the Electric Power System make essential the studies in the area of signal processing applied to digital protection. Generators and transformers are subject to extensive damage, which occurs during faults or improper system operations. These conditions must be quickly identified and eliminated. Thus, the ANSI 24 function is used to protect transformers and generators against overexcitation, where its actuation is given by the percentage value of the Volts/Hertz ratio. Considering that the frequency is one of the parameters used by the referred relay, it can be concluded that the computational tool used to estimate the frequency directly influences the performance of this relay. Thus, this work aims to demonstrate the behavior of function 24 using different frequency estimation methods published in the specialized literature. So, a test system was implemented in the ATPDraw software, in order to simulate overexcitation events. The voltage signal generated in the simulations were processed by the frequency estimators and by the Volts/Hz digital relay logic, which were implemented in Matlab® software. Finally, the results obtained allowed to conclude that, as expected, the frequency estimators directly influence the performance of function 24, causing delays in the operation, as well as the non-functioning or inadequate operation of the Volts/Hertz relays.

articleTitle: Modeling of Small Island Power Systems with Integrated PV and Battery Energy Storage using EMTP-RV
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) generation is a key step toward achieving energy sustainability, especially in Small Island Developing States. However, the nature of distributed solar PV is different to conventional generation and can adversely affect load flows, as well as the voltage and frequency stability of the grid. In this paper, the Tobago power system was modelled along with solar PV generation and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to determine the steady state and dynamic impacts, by performing simulations in Electromagnetic Transients Program, EMTP RV 4.1. Steady state simulations were conducted using various solar PV connection points and load growths, while transient analysis was completed by increasing solar PV penetration levels and testing the system response to different fault locations. An existing load bus was the most suitable location for integrating solar PV since the step-down transformers were currently at risk of overloading. Using this configuration, it was found that the Tobago power system maintained stability up to 30% PV penetration, however the frequency response was affected due to reduction in grid inertia caused by the displacement of synchronous generator machines. The BESS mitigated this effect by providing virtual inertia and frequency regulation.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis in Electric Power System Considering High Penetration of Renewable Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: There is no doubt that renewable generation, especially wind and solar photovoltaic, has many energy and environmental benefits. However, there are many uncertainties related to them to compromise the stable operation of the electrical power system. The penetration of renewable sources has reached records, showing the need for broader studies that make it possible to understand their behavior. To contribute to this area, the present work proposes a study of transient analysis, focusing on electromechanical stability, in a transmission system with a high presence of renewable generation. The WSCC test transmission system was adapted to compose varied scenarios, and the results were analyzed considering the Brazilian grid code.

articleTitle: Technological Architecture Design for Energy Communities: The Colombian Case
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Energy communities (ECs) play an important role in modern energy systems. ECs empower users and facilitate the inclusion of distributed generation, electric vehicles, storage systems, and demand response programs. To know the interoperability of the technologies to be used in the EC with the different areas of the electricity production chain and the actors involved, 5 models of EC for Colombia are proposed with their respective Smart Grid Architecture Model (SGAM) diagram. Furthermore, a series of different gaps that must be considered for the correct development of ECs in the country are identified.

articleTitle: Blockchain in Consumer-Centric Electricity Markets: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The power and energy sector transition into decentralized and distributed models brings a set of challenges that need to be overcome. Among them is consumer empowerment, which requires secure economic transactions and reliable system operation. Thus, new technologies and procedures such as blockchain have gained prominence, due to their reliability and privacy-preserving capabilities. These characteristics are essential for the proliferation of energy community markets. Therefore, this paper provides an overview of blockchain technology applicability to consumer-centric electricity markets, highlighting existing projects and initiatives. Additionally, key enablers and barriers to blockchain deployment in local electricity markets are discussed, followed by a roadmap for the comprehensive adoption of such technology.

articleTitle: High Voltage SF6 Circuit Breaker Selection for a Substation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Modernizing high voltage substations by selecting proper gas circuit breakers is essential to meet the higher demands, new loads, and different load types. It ensures that the electricity supply is reliable and affordable to industrial and commercial customers. The critical issues are the asymmetric fault components on the high voltage side due to different dynamic loading scenarios among the customers. The gas circuit breaker selection must consider all the worst scenarios. This paper investigates a substation of 138 kV transmission and 13.2 kV distribution circuits. At varying dynamic loading, the asymmetrical fault current, critical parameters of the gas circuit breaker like the dc component, and the maximum fault current withstanding ability are analyzed. A procedure is proposed based on the steps required to plan and design a substation. Iteration is performed at different dynamic loading scenarios to select suitable gas circuit breakers to ensure reliable and optimal power flow through the substation.

articleTitle: A MBNLP Method for Centralized Energy Pricing and Scheduling in Local Energy Community
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes a new optimization model for pricing and demand scheduling in a grid-connected local energy community (LEC), including residential homes (consumers and prosumers), and combined heat and power (CHP) generation units. It is assumed that some homes have photovoltaic (PV) generation, electric vehicles (EVs), or both. A central entity is responsible for managing the EVs' charging and discharging process, and for scheduling energy exchanges among homes. Moreover, the central entity is responsible for setting the LEC-price for the energy exchanged between CHP producers and homes, and among homes themselves. We model and solve the problem with a mixed binary non-linear programming (MBNLP) approach with the objective to maximize the total benefit of consumers/prosumers. The LEC-price is set based on demand and supply. The proposed approach is applied to a case study with 100 homes and 5 CHP generation units, and the results are reported for three different electricity grid tariffs A, B, and C. The results suggest 12%, 10% and 23% cost reduction in comparison with not considering the LEC respectively for tariffs A, B, and C.

articleTitle: Digital Twin, Simulation BIM and Virtual Reality Models for Substation Lifecycle in Engineering, Operation, Asset Management & Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: Creating Digital Twin models for already existing substations is one of the big challenges for the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) electrical industry - to reach the goal of digitalization of the assets. The Digital Twin follows all changes and represents the physical twin in a digital model - can be used for simulating, analysis of data, understanding of problems, monitoring and simulation of real-world conditions. To get a Digital Twin with innovative methods and less effort, the Scan to Twin principle is introduced, by creating - out of point clouds - a smart Building Information Modeling (BIM) model and Digital Twin with connections to other databases, as a real Virtual Reality (VR) substation simulation model. This paper describes the process of how to get the models, step by step, with a real use-case of an existing substation project of a transmission operator. The paper introduces a newly developed VR client solution connected to a BIM engineering solution to create - in a few clicks - VR models of existing substation BIM models.

articleTitle: A review on challenges for the dissemination of battery electric vehicles in Brazilian market
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a survey on the main challenges to disseminating battery electric vehicles in the Brazilian power sector and conserving a sustainable position in the market. This research addresses the analysis of the advantages, challenges, and obstacles of the current context in the country, through the study of international public policies and the Brazilian regulatory scenario, given the observation of the significant difference between the introduction of the battery electric vehicle in the world market and Brazil. This paper presents an exploratory meaning which provides the challenges for the spread of electromobility in Brazil.

articleTitle: Grid Code, Part 3: Technical Recommendations and Challenges for Implementing the Rules Book
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)

authors.preferredName: Abigail De La Luz Carrillo Lugo

abstract: This paper presents some recommendations on how to implement a local Rulebook in countries that have not yet established the requirements of electrical parameters their maximum and minimum limits. Since the end of the 90'<tex>$s$</tex> and to date, it has been a gradual implementation within the regions of the planet and in each country the binding laws of the electricity sector that to some extent are voluntary to comply and trace a benefit of Energy Sustainability and Decarbonization. As the interconnection between Transmission System Operators (TSO's) and Independent Energy Producers (PIE's) has been integrated, progress is being made in promoting the use of Variable Renewable Energy Sources or VRE's for its acronym in English Variable Renewables Energy. This has fostered an explicit concern in the countries for not having plant stoppages or abrupt blackouts not scheduled by the interconnection with the Point of Interconnection or “POI” with the TSO; that is, it is necessary a firm intention to establish a Rule Book containing the parameterization established in the maximum and minimum limits and a correlation in the use of alternating current or direct current. The series of these articles has explained the highlights in Part 1, the parameterization of electrical requirements in Part 2 and in this paper the recommendations and challenges to implement the Grid Code in the regions or countries will be described. The intention of this work is to show thechallenges to write the Rule Books for Grid Code and for the benefit of the Energy Sector community.

articleTitle: Electricity Market Simulator to Assess High Shares of Variable Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The high shares of renewable energy create challenges in the operation of electrical systems and in market designs, in this sense, the objective of this work is to develop a model that can simulate an electricity market based on bids, which has generation thermal, hydraulic, variable renewables and battery energy storage systems (BESS) where energy and reserves requirements are co-optimized. It is assumed that the firms compete until reaching the Cournot-Nash Equilibrium in pure strategies, which is obtained through the maximization of the Nikaido-Isoda function and a relaxation algorithm for its solution. In this way, with the results of generation, allocation of reserves and prices, it will be possible to evaluate the market power in systems that already have price offers established, as well as the markets based on costs that wish to migrate to one of offers. Potential mitigation of market power through the establishment of bilateral contracts will also be evaluated. The market simulator will be applied to a modification of the IEEE 24-bus reliability test system and the results obtained will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Threat Scenarios and Monitoring Requirements for Cyber-Physical Systems of Flexibility Markets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The ongoing integration of renewable generation and distributed energy resources introduces new challenges to distribution network operation. Due to the increasing volatility and uncertainty, distribution system operators (DSOs) are seeking concepts to enable more active management and control. Flexibility markets (FMs) offer a platform for economically efficient trading of electricity flexibility between DSOs and other participants. The integration of cyber, physical and market domains of multiple participants makes FMs a system of cyber-physical systems (CPSs). While cross-domain integration sets the foundation for efficient deployment of flexibility, it introduces new physical and cyber vulnerabilities to participants. This work systematically formulates threat scenarios for the CPSs of FMs, revealing several remaining security challenges across all domains. Based on the threat scenarios, unresolved monitoring requirements for secure participation of DSOs in FMs are identified, providing the basis for future works that address these gaps with new technical concepts.

articleTitle: Analysis of performance of photovoltaic systems based on solar irradiation at UPB ecocampus Medellín
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The growing search for alternatives to fossil fuels drives large investments in research and development in non-conventional renewable energy, all this helps to have an increasing number of this kind of projects, creating the need to evaluate their performance and viability. This article aims to carry out a performance analysis of photovoltaic systems in Medellín.

articleTitle: Energy management system: a case study for a campus microgrid
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: This article focuses on developing an energy management system (EMS) for a microgrid on a university campus. The microgrid comprises photovoltaic (PV) systems, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), backup generators, and local loads. The proposed EMS seeks to optimize the power flow, enabling the bidirectional power flow between the microgrid and the utility grid, through a mathematical model and algorithm that establishes BESS charging and discharging patterns, also considering battery degradation via the rainflow algorithm, to minimize energy cost. The EMS is modeled through a Mixed-Integer Conic Programming (MICP) optimization problem aiming at minimizing the operational cost of the university campus. The results obtained showed that the EMS developed reached the proposed objective, minimizing the energy costs of the microgrid when choosing the appropriate device to meet the loads. In addition, potential improvements were identified for the analyzed microgrid, such as expanding the photovoltaic generation system and improving system management strategies and the use of the storage system.

articleTitle: A Novel Protection Coordination Scheme for Regionalized Microgrid at Islanded Mode
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: The modern microgrids are becoming very complex due to the growing penetration levels of renewable distributed generations (RDGs). The integration of RDGs in power system can lead to change in the fault current level and network topologies, which in turn cause the overcurrent and relay coordination issues. Design and selection of a proper protection scheme is very important for reliable and safe operation of microgrid. In this paper, the effect of different penetration levels of renewable DGs and loads has been considered for an adaptive protection coordination scheme of regionalized microgrid. The main focus of this paper is on use of optimization algorithm to obtain maximum current along each line. Based on these values, proper pick-up current setting can be determined for each over-current protection. Case studies have been performed with the different ranges of penetration level of RDGs and load demands. Results have shown the strength of proposed algorithm. This analysis can be very helpful to maintain the reliability and security of the grids with high penetration level of renewable generation.

articleTitle: Learning the optimal joint operation of the energy systems of Uruguay, Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: In the continuous fight against Bellman's Curse of Dimensionality, this work presents the first steps towards learning the Optimal Operation Policy of the electricity generation system of Uruguay, Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina with the infrastructures projected for the year 2030. The Operation Policy under consideration involves 76 state variables: one associated to the surface temperature anomaly of the Pacific Ocean in the N34 area, and 75 related to the hydroelectric reservoirs. The proposed methodology includes the design and training of two alternate neural network architectures combined with modern techniques devised for variance reduction and exploration, which were key to the success achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of China 1000kV UHVAC Power Grid Voltage Security, Operational Flexibility, and Economic Efficiency using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to determine best options for transmission system expansion for UHVAC systems, considering a) voltage security regarding lighting overvoltage, b) operational flexibility using contingency analysis, and c) economics efficiency using machine learning. Inspired by standard contingency analysis, the method provides an integrated ranking approach to synthetize optimal solutions for expansion. The method is integrated using commercial power system software, and it is demonstrated on China's 1000kV UHVAC Power Grid. The validity of the method is verified by the actual decisions included in China's 1000kV UHVAC power grid expansion plan.

articleTitle: Grid Code, Part 2: Global Parameterization and Comparison in the Electricity Sector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Generation, Transmission and Distribution Conference and Exposition – Latin America (IEEE PES GTD Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents the requirements, correlations, trends and global comparisons of the topic of Grid Code in energy systems. The Grid Codes or the guidelines of the electrical systems, began to appear in a generalized way more than 20 years ago around the world, among the Grid Codes of different countries there are certain common specifications, where they formulate the technical and operational characteristics of the different parties involved; that is; from the generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy to ensure the level of quality of the energy supply to be delivered to end-users. There are many rules and policies in each Grid Code that deal with the process involved in the electrical system, establishing a series of requirements to facilitate operational flexibility and stability, security and quality of the electricity supply. The concept of Grid Code is conceptually described as a technical document containing the rules governing the operation, maintenance and development of the electrical system. This paper shows the requirements of typical based on the parameters considered in different regions of the world to have a reliable electrical system in each country under the argument that the systems must comply with the Rule Books. The intention of this work is to show trends in some countries where Rulebooks are applied for Grid Code and compliance with parameters used globally.
